original_question: Does the nonlinear Schrodinger equation posed on a tree graph admit a rigorous well-posedness theory comparable to the star-graph case, beyond the currently available partial results based on dispersive estimates?
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the unlabelled open problem in Section 1.1, stated immediately after the discussion of BBM on trees: 'By the way a result of well posedness of NLS on trees is not yet proven, although well plausible; a step in this direction with proof of relevant dispersive estimates is given in [26,27].' In context, the comparison point is Theorem 1 on star graphs, which gives the relevant well-posedness package for NLS in the energy space.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the paper's tree-graph well-posedness issue, correctly treats it as an open problem rather than an established theorem, correctly uses the star-graph theory as the benchmark, and correctly notes that the available progress cited by the paper is only partial and based on dispersive estimates.
missing_details: The paper is working in the metric-graph setting of Section 1.1, so the object is a metric tree, not an arbitrary combinatorial tree.
The nearby model is the power-type focusing NLS, written in the surrounding discussion as i ∂_t Psi = H Psi - |Psi|^{2 mu} Psi, or equivalently in integral form as equation (1.3).

The comparison with the star-graph case should be made explicit via Theorem 1: local existence and uniqueness in the energy domain E, existence of a maximal solution with the blow-up alternative, conservation of mass and energy, and global existence in the subcritical range 0 < mu < 2.

The relevant function space in the comparison theorem is E, the quadratic-form (energy) domain of the linear Hamiltonian, with time regularity C^0 in E and C^1 in E*; your draft leaves the functional setting implicit.
The linear part is the selfadjoint graph Hamiltonian H determined by vertex conditions; the draft does not specify the operator or the role of vertex conditions at all.

The paper's wording does not make this a question about all nonlinearities; the nearby discussion is centered on power nonlinearities, and global-in-time existence is singled out specifically for 0 < mu < 2.
If 'comparable to the star-graph case' is meant literally, conservation of the mass and energy functionals should be included, not just existence/uniqueness.
The 'currently available partial results' should be identified more precisely as the dispersive-estimate works cited in references [26] and [27], exactly as the paper says.
refined_question:
Let T be a metric tree, let H be the selfadjoint graph Hamiltonian determined by prescribed vertex conditions, and consider the power-type NLS with initial datum Psi(0) = Psi_0 in the energy domain E (the quadratic-form domain of H),
i ∂_t Psi(t) = H Psi(t) - |Psi(t)|^{2 mu} Psi(t).
Can one prove on trees an analogue of the star-graph well-posedness theorem stated in Section 1.1—namely local existence and uniqueness in E, a maximal-lifespan solution satisfying the blow-up alternative, conservation of mass and energy, and, at least for 0 < mu < 2, global well-posedness—thereby extending the then-available results beyond the dispersive estimates cited in [26,27]?
justification: There is no numbered conjecture or officially boxed open problem for this point in the paper; the target is the explicit unlabelled remark in Section 1.1 on the absence of a well-posedness result for NLS on trees. The surrounding context matters: just before that remark, the paper states Theorem 1 for star graphs, including the exact well-posedness features that make the comparison precise. So the sharp, paper-faithful rewrite is not a broad question about NLS on general graphs, standing waves, or scattering, but specifically the extension of the Theorem 1 well-posedness framework from star graphs to metric trees, beyond the partial dispersive-estimate results cited by the author.
